cues: Compare the old file system with a DBMS.
Files repeat data and drift apart; a DBMS stores it once.
Files need a new program for every new question; a DBMS answers any query.
It enforces rules, handles many users at once, and controls who sees what.
The price: cost, complexity, and a trained administrator.
